div.head: ECf 21
div.ab: Barones etiam milites suos et proprios seruientes suos, scilicet dapiferos, pincernas, camerarios, cocos, pistores, sub suo friborgo habebant; et ipsi suos armigeros uel alios seruientes suos sub suo friborgo.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 647 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

div.ab: Barons also had their knights and their own servants, namely stewards, butlers, chamberlains, cooks, bakers, under their own frankpledge; and these their squires or their other servants under their frankpledge.

note.seg: friborg bed. hier 'Haftung des Herrn für den Untergebenen ohne Gegenseitigkeit' s. Zehnerschaft 3c; Bürgschaft 3o—r; Adel 26; Vassallität 19. a. Der Vermögenlose, der nicht in Freibürgschaft war, suchte Schutzherrschaft [ein entflohener Verbrecher war 'not in a tithing, but in the mainpast of R.; therefore R. is in mercy'; Hudson Eastbourne 13]. — Die hier genannten Adelsbeamten (s. d. Gl 2) des Haushalts begegnen am Königshofe als servientes regis; vgl. Round King's serjeants.

friborg here means 'liability of the lord for the subordinate without reciprocity'; see Zehnerschaft 3c; Bürgschaft 3o—r; Adel 26; Vassallität 19. a. The man without property who was not in a frankpledge sought a protecting lordship [an escaped criminal was 'not in a tithing, but in the mainpast of R.; therefore R. is in mercy'; Hudson Eastbourne 13]. — The household officers of the nobility named here (see that word in Gl 2) appear at the king's court as servientes regis; cf. Round King's serjeants.
